title: Bioinspired Spiky Peroxidase-Mimics for Localized Bacterial Capture and Synergistic Catalytic Sterilization

nodes.label: Bacterial wound infection needs an antibiotic-free agent that eradicates bacteria at ultralow dose

requires_unseen: 'antibiotic-free treatment' and the vancomycin comparison stated only in the F7 linked text

nodes.label: A virus-like spiky shell on a cascaded Cu(II)+MoO3 peroxidase-mimic should capture bacteria and kill them by localized ROS

requires_unseen: that the spiky shell plus the Cu(II)+MoO3 cascade is proposed as one 'LCK' strategy before any result is shown (F1/F4 linked text; the name itself is also drawn in the F5a schematic, which is not a measurement)

nodes.label: A Cu(II)-BTC MOF is chosen as the peroxidase-mimetic catalytic core

nodes.label: Phosphomolybdic acid hydrate is loaded into the MOF to add MoO3 cocatalyst centres

nodes.label: A virus-like spiky mesoporous silica shell is targeted on the core to give bacterial capture

requires_unseen: reagents and ambient-temperature step named in F1a and the F1 linked text

Cu and Mo catalytic centres are distributed homogeneously through the POD-M core in both samples

that the DFT surface model stands for the phosphomolybdate-loaded MOF (F3 linked text)

nodes.label: A spiky surface pierces and binds the lipid bilayer far more strongly than a flat surface

Treated wounds regain near-normal CD31 vessel density at 16 d, level with vancomycin

nodes.label: Viruses carry surface spikes that let them attach to and enter host cells

nodes.label: The flat slab still rests on the bilayer at 24 ns, while the spiky tube has passed through it by 16 ns and splayed the lipid tails

attrs.image_note: The two rows are not rendered alike: the bilayer of F6b is already drawn in a looser licorice style at 0 ns, so part of the apparent disorder is a rendering difference. A pulling force is applied to both surfaces, so penetration is force-driven, not spontaneous.

nodes.label: The flat surface plateaus at 4.3 nm and -3000 kJ/mol after about 6 ns, while the spiky surface keeps closing to 1.0 nm and gaining to about -7000 kJ/mol at 24 ns

attrs.image_note: At 15 ns the spiky energy curve reads about -6.2e3 kJ/mol where the linked text says about -6500; the flat plateau starts near 6 ns where the text says 5 ns. Neither spiky curve has reached a plateau at 24 ns.

nodes.label: With POD-M+H2O2 the bacteria sit in clusters away from the particles, while with V-POD-M+H2O2 every bacterium is embedded in the particle aggregate

attrs.image_note: Same reading for both strains; the V-POD-M panels are false-coloured (bacteria yellow, particles grey).

nodes.label: After V-POD-M+H2O2 the bacterial envelopes are broken and the cytoplasm granular, where after V-POD-M alone the envelope is continuous

nodes.label: With V-POD-M+H2O2 the bacteria are all red and gathered into one dense captured patch, where controls are green and evenly scattered

nodes.label: The V-POD-M+H2O2 wound still expands from about 128 to about 197 mm2 by day 1 and measures about 12 mm2 at day 16

notes: One spine: need for antibiotic-free sterilization -> Cu(II)-BTC MOF core with loaded phosphomolybdic acid -> spiky mesoporous silica shell -> two branches (Cu+MoO3 cascade raising .OH output; spiky surface piercing the membrane) meeting at complete bacterial eradication -> rabbit wound closure and tissue recovery at the vancomycin level. Four audits and one limitation, all from the images: F2c shows MoO3 alone oxidizing TMB well above the blank although the linked text says it has no peroxide catalytic activity; F2f shows a large TAOH background in all four groups so the Cu+MoO3 gain is about twofold, not the 'only group with a signal' of the text; F5c annotates 'POD-M structure collapse' after H2O2, an alternative reason for the flat mimic's weak killing that the text never weighs; F7b shows the V-POD-M+H2O2 wound expanding to about 197 mm2 by day 1 and still about 12 mm2 at day 16, against 'no expansion tendency, completely repaired within 15 d'; and F7 carries no POD-M+H2O2 arm at all. Other figure-text mismatches folded into image_note: the TAOH band peaks near 420 nm, not the 435 nm of the F2d caption; F2g has no intensity scale so the 'sixfold' EPR increase cannot be checked; F6d reads about -6.2e3 kJ/mol at 15 ns where the text says -6500 and the flat plateau starts near 6 ns not 5 ns; F4d shows the POD-M+H2O2 fields almost entirely red (dead) although the text calls that group insufficient; the F4f MIC arrow for V-POD-M+H2O2 sits well above the 16 ug/mL quoted in the text. Packet notes: F1 (tier C2_order_violation) and F4 (tier C3_caption_swap) offer no panel crops, so both were read as whole figures and their nodes carry panel_ids []; the F2d crop is tagged cue class 'micrograph' with scale bar True although it is a molecular reaction scheme, so it was not cited.

split_nodes.why: the label stated two claims with two disjoint evidence sets: epidermal thickness (Masson band o19, thickness index o20) and vessel density (CD31 fields o21, CD31/vessel-count bars o22). Re-epithelialization and angiogenesis are different endpoints, so the node could not be graded against either evidence pair.
split_nodes.spine: s17 (the paper's primary histology endpoint, with the quantitative index) stays on the spine; s19 is a side claim, so the spine stays at 18 nodes

merges_considered_and_rejected.why: s16 is the PRF endpoint (wound closed by day 16) and c1 the DSC verdict over both endpoints, with its own premise k3 and its own evidence o16/o22; the vancomycin parity in s16's label is the reading of the F7b curves, not a restatement of c1

different claims from different figures: o11 is the SEM capture geometry (bacteria embedded in the particle aggregate), o13 the live/dead field (all red and gathered). o13 adds the killing dimension that o11 does not carry

each already merges two panels that state one claim (F6c+F6d: flat plateaus, spiky does not; F8d+F8e: the same ranking over the same five groups). Two co-plotted quantities carrying one claim is not two claims, so they are not split back
